## Mo's own task queue, served over MCP. Agents lease a task, check in while
## working, and report it done or failed. A change to anything compiled in,
## meaning this program, job-queue.mo, lib/ or the compiler's output, refuses the
## saved data of a running queue.
module Main
expose JobFilter(..), Page(..), PageError(..), Stats(..), SubmitError(..)
use JobQueue{Queue, Job, QueueError}

max_payload_bytes = 2048
max_jobs = 5000
max_page_jobs = 100
lease_length = 30.minutes
full_advice = "This limit counts every job ever submitted and never falls, so retrying cannot help. Tell a person."

service
  state Queue = JobQueue.empty
  tools submit, lease, heartbeat, acknowledge, fail, list, stats
  every 1.minute expire
  token from env "QUEUE_TOKEN"
end

enum SubmitError
  PayloadTooLarge(limit: Int, bytes: Int)
  QueueFull(limit: Int, advice: Text)
end

enum JobFilter
  AllJobs
  Ready
  Leased
  Done
  Dead
end

enum PageError
  BadPage(after: Int, limit: Int, max_limit: Int)
end

struct Page
  jobs: List(Job)
  next: Option(Int)
  now: Time
end

struct Stats
  total: Int
  ready: Int
  leased: Int
  done: Int
  dead: Int
  limit: Int
  now: Time
end

## Adds a task and returns its id. Every Int in this service, in arguments and
## replies, is a JSON string.
## `payload` is free text handed to a worker unchanged, at most 2,048 bytes. Give
## a short brief and say where the rest is. It is kept for good and any token
## holder can read it, so keep secrets out.
## PayloadTooLarge gives the limit and the size sent: shorten it. HTTP 413 means
## the request body passed 16 KiB, so the payload never reached the queue:
## shorten it.
## QueueFull: the limit of 5,000 counts every job ever submitted, including Done
## and Dead, and never falls. Retrying cannot help, so tell a person.
## Not safe to retry blindly: a retry after a lost reply or store_failed makes a
## second job, so check `list` first.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit. Five
## of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts stop it for
## everyone until a person starts it.
fn submit(queue: Queue, _now: Time, payload: Text) : Result((Queue, Int), SubmitError)
  bytes = payload.byte_count
  return Error(PayloadTooLarge(limit: max_payload_bytes, bytes: bytes)) if bytes > max_payload_bytes
  return Error(QueueFull(limit: max_jobs, advice: full_advice)) if JobQueue.jobs(queue).size >=
    max_jobs
  Ok(JobQueue.submit(queue, payload))
end

## Leases the oldest ready task for 30 minutes and counts an attempt. Replies
## {"case":"None"} when nothing is ready, and nothing will notify you. To look
## without taking anything, use `list`. Wait a minute before calling this again.
## {"case":"Some","value":job} gives you the job. A job is {"id","payload",
## "attempts","state"}, and `state` is {"case":"Ready"}, {"case":"Leased","fields":
## {"until":time}}, {"case":"Done"} or {"case":"Dead"}. Pass `job.id` as `id` and
## `job.attempts` as `attempt` to the other tools, and keep both somewhere that
## survives losing your context: no tool tells you which job is yours. The lease ends at
## `job.state.fields.until`. Call `heartbeat` about every 10 minutes.
## If `job.attempts` is above 1, an earlier attempt ran and may have left partial
## work, so check before starting. The third attempt that fails or expires makes
## the job Dead for good; a coordinator re-submits it as a new job or tells a
## person.
## Never hold a lease while waiting on a person, such as for a PR review: the
## lease runs out and another worker repeats the task. Acknowledge at hand-off.
## Not safe to retry: after a lost reply the job stays held by nobody until the
## lease ends, and one attempt is spent.
## A tool's own refusal is {"error":{"kind":"application","value":{"case":...}}}.
## A runtime error is {"error":{"kind":"runtime","code":...,"message":...,
## "effect":...}}, where `effect` says what this call did to the queue: none,
## applied or unknown. It does not say whether a retry is safe.
## What to do about runtime errors, on every tool:
## - busy, rate_limited: wait, then retry.
## - invalid_arguments: fix the call; do not repeat it.
## - handler_failed, work_limit, memory_limit: never repeat the call, and tell a
##   person. Five of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts
##   stop it for everyone until a person starts it. With effect none, your lease
##   still ends when it did, so keep working inside it.
## - store_failed, or no reply at all: the outcome is unknown, so treat it as a
##   lost reply for that tool.
## - stopped: the service is down until a person starts it. Stop calling and keep
##   your id and attempt.
## - response_limit: on `list`, lower `limit`. On a tool that changes the queue,
##   the change was applied.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  JobQueue.lease(queue, now, lease_length)
end

## Renews your lease for 30 minutes from now without counting an attempt. Call it
## about every 10 minutes while working, and before any step that may block for
## over 20 minutes. `id` is `job.id` and `attempt` is `job.attempts`, both JSON
## strings from `lease`. Safe to retry.
## NotLeased: read the job with `list`, using filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after`
## id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done with your attempt: your acknowledge
## landed, so that is success. Ready or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran
## out, so stop. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than yours: a later attempt
## owns the job, so stop.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.heartbeat(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Marks your leased job Done. A task ends at hand-off: acknowledge when your PR
## opens or your work is delivered, not after a person reviews it. `id` is
## `job.id` and `attempt` is `job.attempts`, both JSON strings from `lease`. Safe
## to retry.
## NotLeased does not mean your work failed: read the job with `list`, using
## filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after` id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done
## with your attempt: your earlier acknowledge landed, so that is success. Ready
## or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran out, so stop and tell the
## coordinator what you delivered. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than
## yours: a later attempt owns the job, so stop and do not acknowledge.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.acknowledge(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Gives your leased job back when you cannot finish it. It goes back to Ready,
## or to Dead on its third attempt, and a Dead job is never retried. The queue
## may hand the same job to the next `lease`. `id` is `job.id` and `attempt` is
## `job.attempts`, both JSON strings from `lease`. Safe to retry.
## NotLeased: read the job with `list`, using filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after`
## id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done with your attempt: an earlier
## acknowledge landed. Ready or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran out or
## your earlier fail landed, so stop. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than
## yours: a later attempt owns the job, so stop.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.fail(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Reads jobs in id order with their payloads, and changes nothing. Safe to
## retry. It is the only way to see the queue, and nothing announces a dead job,
## so a coordinator should list Dead jobs at the start of each cycle.
## All three arguments are required. `filter` is {"case":"X"}, where X is AllJobs,
## Ready, Leased, Done or Dead. `after` is an id: jobs with larger ids are listed,
## so start at "0". `limit` is 1 to 100.
## The reply has `jobs`, `next` and `now`. A job is {"id","payload","attempts",
## "state"}, and `state` is {"case":"Ready"}, {"case":"Leased","fields":
## {"until":time}}, {"case":"Done"} or {"case":"Dead"}. `next` is {"case":"None"}
## on the last page; otherwise pass `next.value` as `after`. `now` is the service's
## clock, for reading each lease's `until`.
## To read one job, use filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after` id - 1 and `limit` 1.
## To count jobs without reading payloads, use `stats`.
## response_limit: lower `limit` and call again. A limit of 1 always fits.
## BadPage: fix the arguments.
## Never pass a job's id and attempts from here to `heartbeat`, `acknowledge` or
## `fail` unless `lease` gave that job to you.
## A dead job's only way back is `submit` with its payload, which makes a new job;
## name the old id in the new payload, because the dead record stays listed.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn list(queue: Queue, now: Time, filter: JobFilter, after: Int, limit: Int) : Result(
  Page,
  PageError
)
  if after < 0 or limit < 1 or limit > max_page_jobs
    return Error(BadPage(after: after, limit: limit, max_limit: max_page_jobs))
  end
  matching = JobQueue.jobs(queue).filter(fn(job) job.id > after and shown?(filter, job) end)
  page = matching.take(limit)
  next = if matching.size > limit: page.last.map(fn(job) job.id end) else: None
  Ok(Page(jobs: page, next: next, now: now))
end

## Counts the jobs in each state, and changes nothing. Safe to retry, and cheap:
## it returns no payloads. Every Int in the reply is a JSON string.
## `total` counts every job ever submitted, including Done and Dead, because jobs
## are never removed. `submit` refuses once `total` reaches `limit`, and that never
## changes, so tell a person when `total` gets close to `limit`.
## `leased` includes leases whose time has passed but that the one-minute expiry
## tick has not returned yet. `now` is the service's clock.
## A coordinator can call this at the start of each cycle, then list Dead jobs
## with `list` when `dead` has grown.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn stats(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Stats
  var ready = 0
  var leased = 0
  var done = 0
  var dead = 0
  for job in JobQueue.jobs(queue)
    case job.state
      JobQueue.Ready: ready += 1
      JobQueue.Leased(until: _): leased += 1
      JobQueue.Done: done += 1
      JobQueue.Dead: dead += 1
    end
  end
  total = ready + leased + done + dead
  Stats(
    total: total,
    ready: ready,
    leased: leased,
    done: done,
    dead: dead,
    limit: max_jobs,
    now: now
  )
end

fn expire(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Queue
  JobQueue.expire(queue, now)
end

fn shown?(filter: JobFilter, job: Job) : Bool
  case filter
    AllJobs: true
    Ready: job.state == JobQueue.Ready
    Leased: job.state is JobQueue.Leased(until: _)
    Done: job.state == JobQueue.Done
    Dead: job.state == JobQueue.Dead
  end
end
## The core of a job queue. Jobs are submitted, leased to a worker for a while,
## and acknowledged when done. A lease that fails or expires puts its job back
## in the queue, up to three attempts in all; after the third, the job is dead.
## The queue is a value: every operation returns the new queue, and no
## operation ever loses a job.
module JobQueue
expose Queue,
Job(..),
JobState(..),
QueueError(..),
empty,
submit,
lease,
heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
expire,
jobs

max_attempts = 3

struct Job
  id: Int
  payload: Text
  attempts: Int
  state: JobState
end

enum JobState
  Ready
  Leased(until: Time)
  Done
  Dead
end

struct Queue
  jobs: Map(Int, Job)
  next_id: Int
end

enum QueueError
  NoSuchJob(id: Int)
  NotLeased(id: Int)
  BadLease(length: Duration)
end

empty = Queue(jobs: {}, next_id: 1)

fn submit(queue: Queue, payload: Text) : (Queue, Int)
  promise "a submitted job is in the queue, ready"
    result.0.jobs.get(result.1) is Some(job) and job.state == Ready
    allows queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (holding([ready(1)]), 1)
    forbids queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (empty, 1)
  end

  id = queue.next_id
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(id, Job(id: id, payload: payload, attempts: 0, state: Ready))
  after.next_id += 1
  (after, id)
end

## Leases the oldest ready job until now + length, counting an attempt. The
## length must be positive, and the lease must end by the year 9999.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time, length: Duration) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  promise "a lease never loses a job"
    result is Ok((after, _)) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(id) after.jobs.has?(id) end)
    allows queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]),
      Some(leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds))
    ))
    forbids queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((empty, None))
  end

  examples
    lease(empty, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((empty, None))
    lease(empty, t0, 0.seconds) == Error(BadLease(length: 0.seconds))
  end

  return Error(BadLease(length: length)) if length <= 0.seconds
  until = try now.checked_add(length).or_fail(BadLease(length: length))
  case queue.jobs.values.find(fn(job) job.state == Ready end)
    None: Ok((queue, None))
    Some(job):
      var taken = job
      taken.state = Leased(until: until)
      taken.attempts += 1
      Ok((put(queue, taken), Some(taken)))
  end
end

## Renews the current lease until now + 30 minutes without counting an attempt.
## NotLeased also covers an expired lease or a different attempt.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be renewed"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  promise "renewing a lease keeps every job and its attempt"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies
      after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        now.checked_add(30.minutes) == Some(until)
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  until = try now.checked_add(30.minutes).or_fail(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))
  var renewed = job
  renewed.state = Leased(until: until)
  Ok(put(queue, renewed))
end

## Finishes a current lease. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be acknowledged"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  promise "acknowledging finishes the job and keeps every job"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.state == Done
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  var finished = job
  finished.state = Done
  Ok(put(queue, finished))
end

## Gives a current lease back after its worker failed: ready again, or dead after
## its last attempt. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can fail"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
  end

  promise "a job is attempted at most three times"
    result is Ok(after) and after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.attempts >= max_attempts implies
      job.state == Dead
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 3)])
    )
  end

  examples
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1)]), t0, 1, 1) == Ok(holding([retried(1, 1)]))
    fail(holding([tried(1, 3)]), t0, 1, 3) == Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    fail(holding([ready(1)]), t0, 1, 0) == Error(NotLeased(id: 1))
    fail(empty, t0, 9, 1) == Error(NoSuchJob(id: 9))
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok(release(queue, job))
end

## Gives back every job whose lease ran out by now, as if its worker failed.
fn expire(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Queue
  examples
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0)]), t0) == holding([retried(1, 1)])
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), t0) == holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)])
  end

  var after = queue
  for job in queue.jobs.values
    if job.state is Leased(until: until) and until <= now
      after = release(after, job)
    end
  end
  after
end

## Every job in the queue, in id order, whatever its state.
fn jobs(queue: Queue) : List(Job)
  examples
    jobs(empty) == []
    jobs(holding([ready(1), done(2)])) == [ready(1), done(2)]
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1), ready(2)]), t0, 1, 1).map(jobs) == Ok([retried(1, 1), ready(2)])
  end

  queue.jobs.values
end

fn leased_job(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Job, QueueError)
  job = try queue.jobs.get(id).or_fail(NoSuchJob(id: id))
  case job.state
    Leased(until: until): if job.attempts == attempt and until > now: Ok(job) else: Error(
      NotLeased(id: id)
    )
    Ready | Done | Dead: Error(NotLeased(id: id))
  end
end

fn release(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var released = job
  released.state = if job.attempts >= max_attempts: Dead else: Ready
  put(queue, released)
end

fn put(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(job.id, job)
  after
end

t0 = Time.parse("2026-10-12T09:00:00Z") or stop "the time is written correctly"

fn holding(jobs: List(Job)) : Queue
  Queue(jobs: jobs.map(fn(job) (job.id, job) end).to_map, next_id: jobs.size + 1)
end

fn ready(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 0, state: Ready)
end

fn leased(id: Int, until: Time) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 1, state: Leased(until: until))
end

fn tried(id: Int, attempts: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: attempts, state: Leased(until: t0 + 30.seconds))
end

fn retried(id: Int, attempts: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: attempts, state: Ready)
end

fn done(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 1, state: Done)
end

fn dead(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 3, state: Dead)
end

test "a job that keeps failing is tried three times, then dead"
  (submitted, id) = submit(empty, "send the invoice")
  var queue = submitted
  for attempt in 1..4
    assert lease(queue, t0, 30.seconds) is Ok((leased_queue, Some(job)))
    assert job.attempts == attempt
    assert fail(leased_queue, t0, id, attempt) is Ok(after)
    queue = after
  end
  assert queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(final)
  assert final.state == Dead
  assert lease(queue, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((queue, None))
end

test "heartbeat renews from now without counting an attempt or changing another job"
  (first, id) = submit(empty, "send the invoice")
  (submitted, other) = submit(first, "publish the report")
  assert lease(submitted, t0, 30.minutes) is Ok((taken, Some(job)))
  now = t0 + 20.minutes
  assert heartbeat(taken, now, id, job.attempts) is Ok(renewed)
  assert renewed.jobs.get(id) is Some(current)
  assert current ==
    Job(id: id, payload: "send the invoice", attempts: 1, state: Leased(until: t0 + 50.minutes))
  assert renewed.jobs.get(other) == submitted.jobs.get(other)
  assert renewed.next_id == submitted.next_id
  assert expire(renewed, t0 + 30.minutes) == renewed
  assert acknowledge(renewed, t0 + 50.minutes - 1.second, id, 1) is Ok(finished)
  assert finished.jobs.get(id) is Some(completed) and completed.state == Done
  assert expire(renewed, t0 + 50.minutes).jobs.get(id) is Some(returned) and returned.state == Ready
  late = Time.parse("9999-12-31T23:40:00Z") or stop "the time is written correctly"
  queue = holding([leased(1, late + 1.second)])
  assert heartbeat(queue, late, 1, 1) == Error(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))
end

test "old attempts cannot change a newer lease"
  (submitted, id) = submit(empty, "send the invoice")
  assert lease(submitted, t0, 30.seconds) is Ok((first, Some(job)))
  returned = expire(first, t0 + 30.seconds)
  now = t0 + 31.seconds
  assert lease(returned, now, 30.seconds) is Ok((second, Some(current)))
  assert current.attempts == 2
  for attempt in [0, job.attempts, 3]
    assert heartbeat(second, now, id, attempt) == Error(NotLeased(id: id))
    assert acknowledge(second, now, id, attempt) == Error(NotLeased(id: id))
    assert fail(second, now, id, attempt) == Error(NotLeased(id: id))
  end
  assert heartbeat(second, now, id, current.attempts) is Ok(renewed)
  assert renewed.jobs.get(id) is Some(extended) and extended.attempts == 2
  assert acknowledge(second, now, id, current.attempts) is Ok(finished)
  assert finished.jobs.get(id) is Some(completed) and completed.state == Done
  assert fail(second, now, id, current.attempts) is Ok(released)
  assert released.jobs.get(id) is Some(retry) and retry.state == Ready and retry.attempts == 2
  queue = holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)])
  assert acknowledge(queue, t0, 1, 1) == Ok(holding([done(1), ready(2)]))

## Simulation tests for the task queue. They live apart from the service so that

fn submit(sim: Simulation, payload: Text) : Int
  return id if Simulation.send(sim, Main.submit, payload) is Ok(Ok((_, id)))
  stop "submit was refused"
end

fn lease(sim: Simulation) : Job
  return job if Simulation.send(sim, Main.lease) is Ok(Ok((_, Some(job))))
  stop "nothing was leased"
end

fn page(sim: Simulation, filter: JobFilter, after: Int, limit: Int) : Page
  return found if Simulation.send(sim, Main.list, filter, after, limit) is Ok(Ok(found))
  stop "list was refused"
end

fn job(sim: Simulation, id: Int) : Job
  page(sim, AllJobs, id - 1, 1).jobs.first or stop "no such job"
end

fn stats(sim: Simulation) : Stats
  return counted if Simulation.send(sim, Main.stats) is Ok(counted)
  stop "stats was refused"
end

fn acknowledged?(sim: Simulation, job: Job) : Bool
  Simulation.send(sim, Main.acknowledge, job.id, job.attempts) is Ok(Ok(_))
end

fn fill(size: Int) : Text
  "x".repeat(size)

## Mo's own task queue, served over MCP. Agents lease a task, check in while
## working, and report it done or failed. A change to anything compiled in,
## meaning this program, job-queue.mo, lib/ or the compiler's output, refuses the
## saved data of a running queue.
module Main
expose JobFilter(..), Page(..), PageError(..), Stats(..), SubmitError(..)
use JobQueue{Queue, Job, QueueError}

max_payload_bytes = 2048
max_jobs = 5000
max_page_jobs = 100
lease_length = 30.minutes
full_advice = "This limit counts every job ever submitted and never falls, so retrying cannot help. Tell a person."

service
  state Queue = JobQueue.empty
  tools submit, lease, heartbeat, acknowledge, fail, list, stats
  every 1.minute expire
  token from env "QUEUE_TOKEN"
end

enum SubmitError
  PayloadTooLarge(limit: Int, bytes: Int)
  QueueFull(limit: Int, advice: Text)
end

enum JobFilter
  AllJobs
  Ready
  Leased
  Done
  Dead
end

enum PageError
  BadPage(after: Int, limit: Int, max_limit: Int)
end

struct Page
  jobs: List(Job)
  next: Option(Int)
  now: Time
end

struct Stats
  total: Int
  ready: Int
  leased: Int
  done: Int
  dead: Int
  limit: Int
  now: Time
end

## Adds a task and returns its id. Every Int in this service, in arguments and
## replies, is a JSON string.
## `payload` is free text handed to a worker unchanged, at most 2,048 bytes. Give
## a short brief and say where the rest is. It is kept for good and any token
## holder can read it, so keep secrets out.
## PayloadTooLarge gives the limit and the size sent: shorten it. HTTP 413 means
## the request body passed 16 KiB, so the payload never reached the queue:
## shorten it.
## QueueFull: the limit of 5,000 counts every job ever submitted, including Done
## and Dead, and never falls. Retrying cannot help, so tell a person.
## Not safe to retry blindly: a retry after a lost reply or store_failed makes a
## second job, so check `list` first.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit. Five
## of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts stop it for
## everyone until a person starts it.
fn submit(queue: Queue, _now: Time, payload: Text) : Result((Queue, Int), SubmitError)
  bytes = payload.byte_count
  return Error(PayloadTooLarge(limit: max_payload_bytes, bytes: bytes)) if bytes > max_payload_bytes
  return Error(QueueFull(limit: max_jobs, advice: full_advice)) if JobQueue.jobs(queue).size >=
    max_jobs
  Ok(JobQueue.submit(queue, payload))
end

## Leases the oldest ready task for 30 minutes and counts an attempt. Replies
## {"case":"None"} when nothing is ready, and nothing will notify you. To look
## without taking anything, use `list`. Wait a minute before calling this again.
## {"case":"Some","value":job} gives you the job. A job is {"id","payload",
## "attempts","state"}, and `state` is {"case":"Ready"}, {"case":"Leased","fields":
## {"until":time}}, {"case":"Done"} or {"case":"Dead"}. Pass `job.id` as `id` and
## `job.attempts` as `attempt` to the other tools, and keep both somewhere that
## survives losing your context: no tool tells you which job is yours. The lease ends at
## `job.state.fields.until`. Call `heartbeat` about every 10 minutes.
## If `job.attempts` is above 1, an earlier attempt ran and may have left partial
## work, so check before starting. The third attempt that fails or expires makes
## the job Dead for good; a coordinator re-submits it as a new job or tells a
## person.
## Never hold a lease while waiting on a person, such as for a PR review: the
## lease runs out and another worker repeats the task. Acknowledge at hand-off.
## Not safe to retry: after a lost reply the job stays held by nobody until the
## lease ends, and one attempt is spent.
## A tool's own refusal is {"error":{"kind":"application","value":{"case":...}}}.
## A runtime error is {"error":{"kind":"runtime","code":...,"message":...,
## "effect":...}}, where `effect` says what this call did to the queue: none,
## applied or unknown. It does not say whether a retry is safe.
## What to do about runtime errors, on every tool:
## - busy, rate_limited: wait, then retry.
## - invalid_arguments: fix the call; do not repeat it.
## - handler_failed, work_limit, memory_limit: never repeat the call, and tell a
##   person. Five of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts
##   stop it for everyone until a person starts it. With effect none, your lease
##   still ends when it did, so keep working inside it.
## - store_failed, or no reply at all: the outcome is unknown, so treat it as a
##   lost reply for that tool.
## - stopped: the service is down until a person starts it. Stop calling and keep
##   your id and attempt.
## - response_limit: on `list`, lower `limit`. On a tool that changes the queue,
##   the change was applied.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  JobQueue.lease(queue, now, lease_length)
end

## Renews your lease for 30 minutes from now without counting an attempt. Call it
## about every 10 minutes while working, and before any step that may block for
## over 20 minutes. `id` is `job.id` and `attempt` is `job.attempts`, both JSON
## strings from `lease`. Safe to retry.
## NotLeased: read the job with `list`, using filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after`
## id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done with your attempt: your acknowledge
## landed, so that is success. Ready or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran
## out, so stop. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than yours: a later attempt
## owns the job, so stop.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.heartbeat(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Marks your leased job Done. A task ends at hand-off: acknowledge when your PR
## opens or your work is delivered, not after a person reviews it. `id` is
## `job.id` and `attempt` is `job.attempts`, both JSON strings from `lease`. Safe
## to retry.
## NotLeased does not mean your work failed: read the job with `list`, using
## filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after` id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done
## with your attempt: your earlier acknowledge landed, so that is success. Ready
## or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran out, so stop and tell the
## coordinator what you delivered. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than
## yours: a later attempt owns the job, so stop and do not acknowledge.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.acknowledge(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Gives your leased job back when you cannot finish it. It goes back to Ready,
## or to Dead on its third attempt, and a Dead job is never retried. The queue
## may hand the same job to the next `lease`. `id` is `job.id` and `attempt` is
## `job.attempts`, both JSON strings from `lease`. Safe to retry.
## NotLeased: read the job with `list`, using filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after`
## id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done with your attempt: an earlier
## acknowledge landed. Ready or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran out or
## your earlier fail landed, so stop. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than
## yours: a later attempt owns the job, so stop.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.fail(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Reads jobs in id order with their payloads, and changes nothing. Safe to
## retry. It is the only way to see the queue, and nothing announces a dead job,
## so a coordinator should list Dead jobs at the start of each cycle.
## All three arguments are required. `filter` is {"case":"X"}, where X is AllJobs,
## Ready, Leased, Done or Dead. `after` is an id: jobs with larger ids are listed,
## so start at "0". `limit` is 1 to 100.
## The reply has `jobs`, `next` and `now`. A job is {"id","payload","attempts",
## "state"}, and `state` is {"case":"Ready"}, {"case":"Leased","fields":
## {"until":time}}, {"case":"Done"} or {"case":"Dead"}. `next` is {"case":"None"}
## on the last page; otherwise pass `next.value` as `after`. `now` is the service's
## clock, for reading each lease's `until`.
## To read one job, use filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after` id - 1 and `limit` 1.
## To count jobs without reading payloads, use `stats`.
## response_limit: lower `limit` and call again. A limit of 1 always fits.
## BadPage: fix the arguments.
## Never pass a job's id and attempts from here to `heartbeat`, `acknowledge` or
## `fail` unless `lease` gave that job to you.
## A dead job's only way back is `submit` with its payload, which makes a new job;
## name the old id in the new payload, because the dead record stays listed.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn list(queue: Queue, now: Time, filter: JobFilter, after: Int, limit: Int) : Result(
  Page,
  PageError
)
  if after < 0 or limit < 1 or limit > max_page_jobs
    return Error(BadPage(after: after, limit: limit, max_limit: max_page_jobs))
  end
  matching = JobQueue.jobs(queue).filter(fn(job) job.id > after and shown?(filter, job) end)
  page = matching.take(limit)
  next = if matching.size > limit: page.last.map(fn(job) job.id end) else: None
  Ok(Page(jobs: page, next: next, now: now))
end

## Counts the jobs in each state, and changes nothing. Safe to retry, and cheap:
## it returns no payloads. Every Int in the reply is a JSON string.
## `total` counts every job ever submitted, including Done and Dead, because jobs
## are never removed. `submit` refuses once `total` reaches `limit`, and that never
## changes, so tell a person when `total` gets close to `limit`.
## `leased` includes leases whose time has passed but that the one-minute expiry
## tick has not returned yet. `now` is the service's clock.
## A coordinator can call this at the start of each cycle, then list Dead jobs
## with `list` when `dead` has grown.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn stats(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Stats
  var ready = 0
  var leased = 0

    ready: ready,
    leased: leased,
    done: done,
    dead: dead,

end

    Leased: job.state is JobQueue.Leased(until: _)
    Done: job.state == JobQueue.Done
    Dead: job.state == JobQueue.Dead

## Run a service

`mo serve FILE --port N --data DIR [--allow-host NAME]` runs the service that the module in `FILE` declares. Check three things first:

- `FILE` has a `service` block. Without one, `mo serve` refuses with E1409, "this module has no service to start". An imported service does not count.
- `DIR` exists. `mo serve` never creates it, so a mistyped path cannot start an empty service. Saved state goes in `DIR/service.sqlite`. `service.sqlite` is readable only by its owner. Only one `mo serve` can use a `DIR` at a time.
- The environment variable named by `token from env "NAME"` holds the access token. A token is 1 to 256 bytes of letters, digits and `-._~+/`, and may end in `=` padding. A missing or invalid token is E1409, and the message names the variable.

`--port` takes 0 to 65535. Port 0 picks a free port. `mo serve` listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It takes no address flag. `--allow-host NAME` also accepts requests whose `Host` is `NAME`, as a proxy in front of the server sends. A `NAME` without a port means port 80. A malformed `NAME` is E1409, "the server configuration was refused". The flag never changes which saved data the program recovers.

The requests below call this service, saved as `counter.mo`:

```text
module Counter

service
  state Int = 0
  tools add, read
  token from env "COUNTER_TOKEN"
end

## Adds an amount to the count.
fn add(state: Int, _now: Time, amount: Int) : (Int, Int)
  (state + amount, state + amount)
end

## Reads the count.
fn read(state: Int, _now: Time) : Text
  state.to_text
end
```

```text
mo serve: listening on http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp
```

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"demo","version":"1"}}}'
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"add","arguments":{"amount":"5"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read"}}
```

`mo serve` writes one line to standard error for each failure, restart and stop, in exactly these formats:

```text
mo serve: failure: NAME: REASON
mo serve: restart: N of M: REASON
mo serve: stop: REASON
```

`NAME` is the tool or timer that failed, as the source writes it, such as `halt` or `tick`. A bad interval names its timer. A saved message that replay runs and rejects, because its handler failed or its result failed the checksum, names its tool or timer. A record refused before it runs, because it is malformed, out of sequence or from a different program, is `service`. `NAME` is the word `service` when no tool or timer is responsible, as when the state's initial value fails, or the store or saved data fails at startup. `mo check` refuses `service` as a tool or timer name, so the word never means a real handler. `NAME` never holds a colon, and `REASON` is always one line. A store that will not open is E1409 with no `failure` line. A store another process holds, such as a second `mo serve` or a reader of `DIR`, is not E1409: `mo serve` waits up to 10 seconds for it, then prints one `mo serve: could not open saved state at` line and exits 75. `N` is this restart's place among the restarts of the last ten minutes, and `M` is the limit of 3, so `3 of 3` is followed by the stop line. A store failure while the service runs is a `stop` line with no `failure` line. A failure that is a bug adds the report `mo run` would print after its line, except during replay. The report's values can quote these words, so anchor a search as `^mo serve: failure:`. Read journald with `journalctl -o cat`, so each line keeps its start. The lines have no timestamps. These line shapes are stable, and changing one is a breaking change. The words of `REASON` are not stable, so branch on the line's kind, on `NAME` and on the exit status. The token never appears in output, logs or errors.

`mo serve` exits with one of these statuses:

- 0: SIGTERM or SIGINT stopped it. It closes its port, so a new connection is refused, and finishes the open ones first, which their deadlines bound to about 25 seconds.
- 1: the program has errors, or it could not start (E1409).
- 2: a mistake in the command.
- 69: supervision (D308) stopped the service. Five failures within a minute restart it, and three restarts within ten minutes stop it. It stays down until a person starts it, as Recover from a stop says.
- 70: it died any other way, such as a failed save, a listener failure or a bug in a module constant. Starting it again is safe.
- 75: another process held the store for the whole wait. Nothing was changed, and starting it again is safe, so a service manager should retry it.

`DIR` records the canonical source bundle, its digest, and the build and state identities alongside the saved state. The first `mo serve FILE --data DIR --port N` records the program atomically with its initial snapshot. Thereafter `mo serve --data DIR --port N` compiles the recorded program and starts it. A new executable build must verify every replayed state checksum before recording its build identity, even if the service image key is unchanged. The previous program identity is retained so failures captured under either build remain attributable. A recorded program that no longer compiles is refused; keep the recording executable for recovery.

A legacy folder with no recorded program can be adopted when its compiled image matches. For a different image, `--adopt` explicitly permits verified replay. An empty tail verifies zero messages and provides no evidence about changed handler behavior. Adoption is not a substitute for migrating an incompatible state schema.

Use the folder after a prior migration so the check can read its recorded source and validated generated declarations. The check does not write to the folder. Exit 0 means the source and migration signature checks passed; it does not mean a migration ran over the folder's state.
- With the service stopped, run `mo serve NEW --data DIR --port N --upgrade [--migrate Module.function]`. Matching saved schemas need no migration. A changed schema needs a pure, non-generic function taking exactly one old state and returning exactly the new service state. Import generated old declarations from `UpgradeOld`; they come from the recorded program, never a candidate disk module. Changed access clauses are refused.

The checked restart replays the old state, runs the migration within restart budgets, validates the result and records the new program and snapshot in one activation transaction. A refused migration leaves the old program and state authoritative. After a successful activation, folder-only startup runs the new program without rerunning the migration. Generated old declarations needed to compile it are retained with the program separately from its source identity, including across later tool-only upgrades. Use it for a migration the live budget refuses.

Source-only `mo check` and `mo test` do not automatically load a recorded program's generated `UpgradeOld` declarations. Use a data-folder base for upgrade checks. `mo replay --failure ID --data DIR` without `FILE` replays a failure under the program the folder retained for it, chosen by image key, build and schema, with its generated declarations. When retained programs with different sources match, it refuses with E1431; give `FILE` then.

## Upgrade a running service

Start the service with a second credential: `mo serve --data DIR --port N --upgrade-token-env NAME`. The value must be at least 16 bytes and differ from the service token; without the option every upgrade tool call is refused with E1414. The service token alone never authorizes an upgrade, and neither credential appears in output, events or the data folder.

On the service host, or through a loopback tunnel to it, run `mo push NEW --url http://127.0.0.1:N/mcp --base DIGEST --token-env NAME --upgrade-token-env NAME [--migrate Module.function] [--json]`. The URL must be plain HTTP to a loopback address; any other URL is refused before either credential is read. `DIGEST` is the source digest of the active program: `mo check NEW --upgrade-from OLD --json` prints it as `base_source`, and a push naming the wrong base is refused with E1416 naming the active digest. The push uploads the source bundle, which the service compiles in a child process while it keeps serving, then checks the candidate against the running program as the checked restart does, migrates the current state under the live budget (1,048,576 work units, 32 MiB), and activates it between two messages in one transaction. Queued calls continue under the new program in order; a queued call to a tool the candidate removed or retyped is answered with the runtime error `removed_by_upgrade` and has no effect; a queued tick of a removed timer is dropped. Timers keep their next due time by name. Exit 0 means the service runs the candidate; the report gives the activation `ordinal`. Pushing the active program again reports `already active` and changes nothing, so a push whose reply was lost is safe to repeat. Exit 1 means a refusal or client failure; exit 2 means invalid command usage, URL or base digest. A refusal names its E14xx code and leaves the old program serving. After activation there is no rollback: a fault in the new program is fixed by another push or, with the service stopped, a checked restart.

Initialize returns an `MCP-Session-Id`. A client that sends it on `GET /mcp` with `Accept: text/event-stream` receives `notifications/tools/list_changed` after each activation; each session has one stream, and a new GET replaces it. Notifications are not a durable log: a reconnecting client calls `tools/list`. POST calls work with or without the session header.

If a checked restart is refused and the program cannot be repaired within those checks, use the fresh-folder fallback. Start the old program on the old `DIR`, read what you need through its tools, and stop it. Start the fixed program on a new, empty `DIR` and send that data to its tools. State that no tool returns stays behind, so keep the old source, executable and data folder.

## Work in this loop

Follow these steps.

1. Write the program. When a function has `examples` or a `promise`, put each block at the top of the body, then a blank line, then the code. Add a `test` in the same file when you check a scenario. Section 12.
2. Run `mo format` on those files.
3. Run `mo check FILE`. It reports each error it finds, in source order. Fix every error it reports before you run `mo check` again, not only the first. Handle E1103 and E1150 as Know this build says.
4. Run `mo fix FILE` when `mo check` shows a fix. When an error shows more than one fix, choose one and make that edit yourself. Appendix A.
5. Run `mo test FILE` only once `mo check` reports no errors but those Know this build names. While the program has other errors, `mo test` runs nothing and prints the same errors `mo check` does. Run `mo test FILE` until the examples, promises, tests, and recovery checks pass.
6. Run `mo run FILE` only when the task needs a running program.

If a command exits 1 for a reason that Know this build names, follow its instructions above, and continue. Section 13.4 describes `--json`.

## Stop when the task is done

The task is done when the program is the v0.1 Mo the reference describes for what it computes, including the specs and tests that behavior needs, and you have run the loop steps this build implements.

On a complete toolchain, `mo format`, `mo check`, and `mo test` exit 0. Run `mo run` when the task is a running program.

On this build, accept a remaining diagnostic only when Know this build names it: E1103 or E1150 on a form the reference requires and offers no other way to write the same behaviour, or E1400 on a promise whose inputs `mo test` cannot build. Deleting a required spec, promise or capability to silence a diagnostic leaves the task undone. Deleting a promise because `mo test` returns E1400 leaves the task undone.

E1408 is also an expected build limitation when `mo run` targets a service entry module. Use `mo serve` to run the service. Use `Simulation` in tests for scheduling and persistence, or test ordinary handlers directly for their value logic. Simulation provides no networking or deployment.

Where the reference says nothing, do not add a rule, and do not fill that silence from the architecture or from `formal/TRANSLATION.md`.

Section 12 shows the form of a spec. When the task is a program, read section 11.2 for `main`'s result and the program's exit status.

### Fetch a private state artifact on the service host

Run `mo fetch http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp --export state --out state.moex --token-env SERVICE_TOKEN`
on the host running the persistent service. The destination must not exist (including a symlink).
The command accepts plain HTTP loopback URLs only, ignores proxies and refuses redirects.
It verifies one complete export generation and publishes a mode-0600 artifact. A failed or
interrupted attempt removes its temporary file; retry creates a new generation. The largest
state requires 2049 pages, about 103 seconds at the service's call rate limit. The largest
failure pair requires 2176 pages, about 109 seconds.
Pin creation, reading the final page (which releases the pin), and publishing the verified local
file are separate events. Repeated creation may observe different state. Use `mo-failures` to
list retained diagnostics and `--export failure ID` to fetch a retained failure pair with the same
verification and private-file publication rules.

### Diagnose a failure offline

These commands run on the service host and start no service. Run them as the service's user, or
first copy the whole stopped data folder, including any `service.sqlite-journal` beside the
database. Never copy `service.sqlite` alone.

`mo history DIR` shows what a stopped data folder holds, and runs no Mo code and no timer. It
shows the last snapshot "as of sequence S, K later messages not applied", the log tail's
sequence, handler index, arrival and argument sizes, and each retained failure with its build and
whether this build can replay it. The log keeps a handler's index, not its name, so a tail entry
says "name not recorded in the log". Messages before the snapshot are gone, so a message missing
from the tail may still have run. A store from before failure capture says "this store predates
failure capture". `mo history` refuses at once, with its own message, a folder a running service
owns, a folder it cannot read, and a folder with no saved data. A journal left by an unfinished
write needs a rollback: run it again as the folder's owner with `--recover`, which writes
database pages but changes no record.

`mo replay FILE --failure ID --data DIR` runs the failed handler again on its recorded state,
arrival time and arguments; `--export failure.moex` reads a fetched artifact instead of `DIR`. It
prints the original message, the pre-call state, the recorded and offline signatures and the
regenerated stack with the top frame's variables. `FILE` must be the untouched source the service
ran, so use the deployed `/opt/mo/$SHA` tree: any byte change, a comment or `mo format` included,
changes the program identity and is refused. Replay also needs the `mo` executable that recorded
the failure: `mo history` shows each record's build digest, and
`sha256sum /opt/mo/*/build/gcc/debug/mo` finds the executable with that digest. Records from a
build without `mo replay` cannot be replayed. The
outcome is `reproduced` (exit 0), or `different`, `not_reproduced` or `refused` (exit 1). A memory
failure that depended on arguments queued in the mailbox does not recur offline, and the outcome
says so.

To check a fix, copy the program's folder, edit the copy, and add `--fix COPY/main.mo`. Both
programs are checked before anything runs, so a fix that changes the state type, or the handler's
name, kind, arguments or result shape, is refused. The original replays first, then the revised
handler runs on the same inputs and budgets. The verdict is `verified` (exit 0) only when the
original reproduced and the revision succeeded within the recorded budgets; otherwise it is
`not_fixed`, `unverified` or `refused` (exit 1). `verified` says the failure is gone, not that the
revision does the right work: the revised outcome shows its reply kind and whether the state
changed.

`mo query FILE FUNCTION --export state.moex` runs a function of yours over an exported state:
`FUNCTION(state)`. `mo query FILE FUNCTION --failure ID --data DIR` (or `--export failure.moex`)
runs it over a failure's inputs: `FUNCTION(state, time, arguments...)` in the handler's order.
`FUNCTION` is a function of `FILE`'s main module, or `Module.name`, exposed or not. `FILE` may add
functions or modules to the deployed program, but the state type must not change, and the input
must come from this `mo` build. The function is not generic (E1410), holds no capability or
function in its parameters or result (E1411), takes the main service's state type first (E1412)
and then exactly the inputs above (E1413). A query runs under `--max-work N` instructions, by
default 1073741824, and `--max-heap`, `--max-stack` and `--max-depth` as `mo run` does; a query
that stops on one exits 70 with a report that names the limit. The result prints as structural
text, or as JSON with `--json`.

`--recover` on `mo replay` and `mo query` means what it means on `mo history`: run as the
folder's owner, it rolls back a journal left by an unfinished write, which writes database pages
but changes no record. It goes with `--data DIR`, never with `--export`.

A refusal prints one `mo replay: refused: CHECK: ...` line, or `mo query: refused:`, naming what
differs with its recorded and found values, and exits 1. No handler or query function runs
before every check passes. The checks run in a fixed order: the input, its build, the program and its
handler, the types, then a fix and the budgets; only the first that fails is named. `mo query`
does not check the program. `CHECK` names are stable; the words after them are not, so branch
on `CHECK`.

| `CHECK` | What differs | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | The artifact or record cannot be read, is not a regular file, or its state does not belong to its message | Fetch the artifact again, or copy the stopped folder again |
| `kind` | A state export given with `--failure`, or a failure without it | Fetch the other kind, or add or drop `--failure ID` |
| `folder` | The data folder cannot be read, as `mo history` would say | Read its message; `--recover` for a journal |
| `failure` | No record with that ID: the folder lists the IDs it keeps, an artifact holds another | Pick a listed ID from `mo history DIR` |
| `build` | Another `mo` build recorded it, or the record names no build | Run the `mo` whose digest `sha256sum` matches |
| `program` | `FILE` is not the untouched deployed source, or declares no service | Use the deployed `/opt/mo/$SHA` tree |
| `handler` | `FILE`'s service has no handler of the recorded name, kind and arguments; for `mo query`, also no service | Use the deployed source, or keep the handler in `FILE` |
| `run` | No memory for the checks | Free memory and run again |
| `state_schema` | `FILE`'s state type differs from the recorded state's | Keep the deployed state type in `FILE` |
| `argument_schema` | A handler or query argument's type differs from the recorded one | Match the handler's argument types |
| `revised_program` | `REVISED` does not compile (its diagnostics come first) or declares no service | Fix it until `mo check REVISED` passes |
| `revised_state_schema` | The fix changes the state type | Keep the state type |
| `revised_handler` | The fix renames the handler or changes its kind, result shape class or arguments | Keep the handler's name and shape |
| `budgets` | The record's budgets differ from this build's, so it is damaged or crafted | Copy or fetch the record again |

Parse `--json`, not text: a text refusal goes to stderr, and `--json` writes every record to
stdout. `--json` writes a version record, one record per outcome (`original`, `revised`, `query`
or `history`), and a totals record whose `status` is the exit status. The fields to branch on are
`outcome` on `original` (`reproduced`, `different`, `not_reproduced`, `refused`) and on `query`
(`returned`, `refused`, `stopped`, with `limit` naming the limit); `verdict` on `revised`;
`refusal.check`, `refusal.recorded` and `refusal.found` on a refused check; `run.status` and
`note` on `original`, where `note` is non-null only when a memory failure did not recur; and, on
`history`, `folder` (`ok`, or why not, as `owned` or `recovery_required`), each failure's `id`
and `replayable_here`.

### Rehearse an upgrade offline

`mo rehearse --artifact EXPORT --old-bundle OLD --candidate NEW
[--migrate Module.function] [--context OLD.mocc] [--json]` reads a state export

## The core of a job queue. Jobs are submitted, leased to a worker for a while,
## and acknowledged when done. A lease that fails or expires puts its job back
## in the queue, up to three attempts in all; after the third, the job is dead.
## The queue is a value: every operation returns the new queue, and no
## operation ever loses a job.
module JobQueue
expose Queue,
Job(..),
JobState(..),
QueueError(..),
empty,
submit,
lease,
heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
expire,
jobs

max_attempts = 3

struct Job
  id: Int
  payload: Text
  attempts: Int
  state: JobState
end

enum JobState
  Ready
  Leased(until: Time)
  Done
  Dead
end

struct Queue
  jobs: Map(Int, Job)
  next_id: Int
end

enum QueueError
  NoSuchJob(id: Int)
  NotLeased(id: Int)
  BadLease(length: Duration)
end

empty = Queue(jobs: {}, next_id: 1)

fn submit(queue: Queue, payload: Text) : (Queue, Int)
  promise "a submitted job is in the queue, ready"
    result.0.jobs.get(result.1) is Some(job) and job.state == Ready
    allows queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (holding([ready(1)]), 1)
    forbids queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (empty, 1)
  end

  id = queue.next_id
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(id, Job(id: id, payload: payload, attempts: 0, state: Ready))
  after.next_id += 1
  (after, id)
end

## Leases the oldest ready job until now + length, counting an attempt. The
## length must be positive, and the lease must end by the year 9999.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time, length: Duration) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  promise "a lease never loses a job"
    result is Ok((after, _)) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(id) after.jobs.has?(id) end)
    allows queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]),
      Some(leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds))
    ))
    forbids queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((empty, None))
  end

  examples
    lease(empty, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((empty, None))
    lease(empty, t0, 0.seconds) == Error(BadLease(length: 0.seconds))
  end

  return Error(BadLease(length: length)) if length <= 0.seconds
  until = try now.checked_add(length).or_fail(BadLease(length: length))
  case queue.jobs.values.find(fn(job) job.state == Ready end)
    None: Ok((queue, None))
    Some(job):
      var taken = job
      taken.state = Leased(until: until)
      taken.attempts += 1
      Ok((put(queue, taken), Some(taken)))
  end
end

## Renews the current lease until now + 30 minutes without counting an attempt.
## NotLeased also covers an expired lease or a different attempt.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be renewed"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  promise "renewing a lease keeps every job and its attempt"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies
      after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        now.checked_add(30.minutes) == Some(until)
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  until = try now.checked_add(30.minutes).or_fail(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))
  var renewed = job
  renewed.state = Leased(until: until)
  Ok(put(queue, renewed))
end

## Finishes a current lease. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be acknowledged"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  promise "acknowledging finishes the job and keeps every job"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.state == Done
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  var finished = job
  finished.state = Done
  Ok(put(queue, finished))
end

## Gives a current lease back after its worker failed: ready again, or dead after
## its last attempt. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can fail"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
  end

  promise "a job is attempted at most three times"
    result is Ok(after) and after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.attempts >= max_attempts implies
      job.state == Dead
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 3)])
    )
  end

  examples
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1)]), t0, 1, 1) == Ok(holding([retried(1, 1)]))
    fail(holding([tried(1, 3)]), t0, 1, 3) == Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    fail(holding([ready(1)]), t0, 1, 0) == Error(NotLeased(id: 1))
    fail(empty, t0, 9, 1) == Error(NoSuchJob(id: 9))
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok(release(queue, job))
end

## Gives back every job whose lease ran out by now, as if its worker failed.
fn expire(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Queue
  examples
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0)]), t0) == holding([retried(1, 1)])
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), t0) == holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)])
  end

  var after = queue
  for job in queue.jobs.values
    if job.state is Leased(until: until) and until <= now
      after = release(after, job)
    end
  end
  after
end

## Every job in the queue, in id order, whatever its state.
fn jobs(queue: Queue) : List(Job)
  examples
    jobs(empty) == []
    jobs(holding([ready(1), done(2)])) == [ready(1), done(2)]
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1), ready(2)]), t0, 1, 1).map(jobs) == Ok([retried(1, 1), ready(2)])
  end

  queue.jobs.values
end

fn leased_job(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Job, QueueError)
  job = try queue.jobs.get(id).or_fail(NoSuchJob(id: id))
  case job.state
    Leased(until: until): if job.attempts == attempt and until > now: Ok(job) else: Error(
      NotLeased(id: id)
    )
    Ready | Done | Dead: Error(NotLeased(id: id))
  end
end

fn release(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var released = job
  released.state = if job.attempts >= max_attempts: Dead else: Ready
  put(queue, released)
end

fn put(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(job.id, job)
  after
end

t0 = Time.parse("2026-10-12T09:00:00Z") or stop "the time is written correctly"

fn holding(jobs: List(Job)) : Queue
  Queue(jobs: jobs.map(fn(job) (job.id, job) end).to_map, next_id: jobs.size + 1)
end

fn ready(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 0, state: Ready)
end

fn leased(id: Int, until: Time) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 1, state: Leased(until: until))
end

fn tried(id: Int, attempts: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: attempts, state: Leased(until: t0 + 30.seconds))
end

fn retried(id: Int, attempts: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: attempts, state: Ready)
end

fn done(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 1, state: Done)
end

fn dead(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 3, state: Dead)
end

## Upgrade a running service

Start the service with a second credential: `mo serve --data DIR --port N --upgrade-token-env NAME`. The value must be at least 16 bytes and differ from the service token; without the option every upgrade tool call is refused with E1414. The service token alone never authorizes an upgrade, and neither credential appears in output, events or the data folder.

On the service host, or through a loopback tunnel to it, run `mo push NEW --url http://127.0.0.1:N/mcp --base DIGEST --token-env NAME --upgrade-token-env NAME [--migrate Module.function] [--json]`. The URL must be plain HTTP to a loopback address; any other URL is refused before either credential is read. `DIGEST` is the source digest of the active program: `mo check NEW --upgrade-from OLD --json` prints it as `base_source`, and a push naming the wrong base is refused with E1416 naming the active digest. The push uploads the source bundle, which the service compiles in a child process while it keeps serving, then checks the candidate against the running program as the checked restart does, migrates the current state under the live budget (1,048,576 work units, 32 MiB), and activates it between two messages in one transaction. Queued calls continue under the new program in order; a queued call to a tool the candidate removed or retyped is answered with the runtime error `removed_by_upgrade` and has no effect; a queued tick of a removed timer is dropped. Timers keep their next due time by name. Exit 0 means the service runs the candidate; the report gives the activation `ordinal`. Pushing the active program again reports `already active` and changes nothing, so a push whose reply was lost is safe to repeat. Exit 1 means a refusal or client failure; exit 2 means invalid command usage, URL or base digest. A refusal names its E14xx code and leaves the old program serving. After activation there is no rollback: a fault in the new program is fixed by another push or, with the service stopped, a checked restart.

Initialize returns an `MCP-Session-Id`. A client that sends it on `GET /mcp` with `Accept: text/event-stream` receives `notifications/tools/list_changed` after each activation; each session has one stream, and a new GET replaces it. Notifications are not a durable log: a reconnecting client calls `tools/list`. POST calls work with or without the session header.

If a checked restart is refused and the program cannot be repaired within those checks, use the fresh-folder fallback. Start the old program on the old `DIR`, read what you need through its tools, and stop it. Start the fixed program on a new, empty `DIR` and send that data to its tools. ## Work in this loop

Follow these steps.

1. Write the program. When a function has `examples` or a `promise`, put each block at the top of the body, then a blank line, then the code. Add a `test` in the same file when you check a scenario. Section 12.
2. Run `mo format` on those files.
3. Run `mo check FILE`. It reports each error it finds, in source order. Fix every error it reports before you run `mo check` again, not only the first. Handle E1103 and E1150 as Know this build says.
4. Run `mo fix FILE` when `mo check` shows a fix. When an error shows more than one fix, choose one and make that edit yourself. Appendix A.

The task is done when the program is the v0.1 Mo the reference describes for what it computes, including the specs and tests that behavior needs, and you have run the loop steps this build implements.

### 11.5 Service blocks

This build checks service blocks. `mo run` of a service entry module still reports E1408; see the end of this section.

A module may declare one top-level `service ... end` block. Its clauses name
the state type and start value, local functions offered as tools, timer
handlers, and the environment variable holding its access token.
`service` is reserved. The clause words `state`, `tools`, `every`, `token`,
`from` and `env` remain ordinary identifiers outside their clause positions.

Clauses occur in this order: exactly one `state`, exactly one `tools` naming
at least one function, zero or more `every` clauses, and exactly one `token`
last. Empty services and timer-only services are refused. No function name
may appear twice anywhere in the block, including across tools and timers.

```mo
module Counter

service
  state Int = 0
  tools increment, snapshots
  every 1.minute tick
  token from env "COUNTER_TOKEN"
end

fn increment(state: Int, _now: Time, amount: Int) : (Int, Bool)
  (state + amount, true)
end

fn snapshots(state: Int, _now: Time) : List(Int)
  [state]
end

fn tick(state: Int, _now: Time) : Int
  state + 1
end
```

The start value has the declared state type. The runtime uses it only when
there is no saved state. Each tool is a function declared in this module
whose first two parameters are the state type and `Time`, the moment the message arrived.
The service selects the local overload whose first parameter exactly matches
its state type, then requires that signature to contain no unresolved generic
parameters. Generic helpers can be called through concrete wrappers. A service
block has no explicit generic-specialization syntax. The state, handler inputs
and handler results must contain neither capabilities nor function values,
including inside records, choices, tuples and collections.

Tool names cannot end in `?` (E0106). Arguments after State and Time, the reply
and any application error must have visible fields and cases, including nested
types (E0105). Imported wire types need their representation exposed with `(..)`;
types declared in this module are visible locally. Private service state need
not be exposed. These wire checks run after the bare-state result check E0101.

A tool updates stored state only when it returns `(State, Reply)` or
`Result((State, Reply), E)`. Returning exactly `State`, or `Result(State, E)`, is an error.
For a bare `State` result, the error offers two fixes: return `(state, Unit)` to
update state, or wrap the value in a record to return it as read-only data.
`Result(State, E)` receives no fixes. `mo fix` applies neither alternative.
The suggested adapters retain the tool's name and `##` comment, rename the
original function to a helper, and rebind the module's references to that
helper. A function on the module's `expose` line receives no fixes, because a
fix can't update callers in other modules. Nor does a function whose name ends
in `?`: it must return `Bool` (section 2.3), so neither adapter could keep its name.
Every other result shape is a read-only reply,
including `List(State)`, `Option(State)` and records containing state.
Read-only messages are neither logged nor saved. Logged and saved mean the
service's state and its recovery log: a record of a failed call kept for
diagnosis (section 13.4) is neither, and keeping one never changes the state,
the log or what recovery restores.

Each `every` clause has a duration literal with a whole-number value of at
least 1, such as `1.minute` or `30.seconds`, and a local handler with exactly
the signature `(State, Time): State`. Simultaneous ticks follow the source
order of the `every` clauses. Unlike a tool returning bare state, a timer
handler returns replacement state. Handlers remain ordinary functions that
examples, promises and tests can call directly.

The token source is a plain text literal naming an environment variable. The
name is nonempty and contains only uppercase ASCII letters, digits and `_`,
and cannot start with a digit. Checking does not read that variable or run a
service. This build checks, tests, formats and fixes service modules, but
`mo run` of a service entry module reports E1408, "mo run does not start
services yet". Importing a service module does not start it.

`mo serve` (section 13.4) exposes a service through authenticated MCP over
